summary:
Our project is a multiplayer lunar base survival game where players work together as a crew to survive five days on the Moon. Players explore different parts of the base, including communications, solar panels, the power house, and the habitat. As the mission progresses, they'll face challenges involving power management, radiation exposure etc. The goal is to make it through each day by working together, managing limited resources, and making decisions that affect the entire crew.

We wanted to create something that gives people a better understanding of the challenges astronauts could face while living on the Moon. Space exploration isn't just about getting there; it's also about keeping people safe and making sure everything they depend on continues working.
details:
Our project is a multiplayer lunar base survival game developed in Unity using C#. The main idea is to have players work together as a crew to survive on the Moon by exploring and maintaining different sections of their lunar base. These sections include communications, solar panels, the power house, and the habitat. Our original plan was to have a five-day mission, with each day introducing new challenges involving electrical power, oxygen, radiation exposure, and resource management.

Although we weren't able to finish every planned feature or fully implement all five days of gameplay, we were able to develop the main concept and build the foundation of the experience. Players can explore the base, experience the multiplayer environment, and see how its different sections would fit into a larger survival mission. We also planned an interactive terminal that would allow players to monitor and control the base's systems as the mission progresses.

We used Unity, C#, Netcode for GameObjects, and Unity Multiplayer Services to develop the game and its multiplayer functionality. We also explored NASA's public data resources, including DONKI and RadLab, to investigate ways of connecting our radiation and space-weather mechanics to real space research.

What makes our project creative is that it approaches lunar exploration as a cooperative survival experience rather than simply an exploration game. The goal is for players to depend on each other, make decisions as a team, and manage limited resources to keep their base operational. Even though the final game doesn't include every feature we originally envisioned, we hope the concept gives people a better understanding of the challenges astronauts could face when living and working on the Moon.
